candidate.title: DNase-Seq / DNaseI-Seq
candidate.scope: Shared explanatory schematic of DNase I hypersensitive-site sequencing in the middle row of the supplied DNA Protein Interactions crop. The row explicitly groups DNase-Seq and DNaseI-Seq, and the matching collection-page heading treats them as alternative assay-family names; both names are retained because their poster-listed references describe distinguishable implementations. This extraction follows the one drawn route, without branching or pooling. At left, the caption DNase I hypersensitive sites sequencing (DNase-Seq, DNaseI-Seq) accompanies an explanatory chromatin icon; no arrow makes that icon a separate preparation. The neighboring ChIP-Seq/ChIP-exo/HT-ChIP/Mint-ChIP and DNaseI-SIM rows are outside this card. The depicted endpoint is extracted DNA. Primary-paper library/readout details clarify that endpoint and the misleading trimmed-complex icon; they do not add unshown operations, GeF-seq, or single-cell adaptations.

states.label: Active chromatin containing exposed genomic DNA and nucleosomes
features: Biological target: chromatin accessibility/DNase I hypersensitivity and relative DNA protection; chemical substrate: genomic DNA within chromatin.

operations.label: DNase I digestion
operations.description: DNase I acts on chromatin DNA, creating cuts and DNA fragments while the cartoon retains protein-associated portions. Accessible positions are more readily cleaved than protected positions. DNase I is the nuclease reagent, not a produced material.
operations.mechanism: Enzymatic cleavage of genomic DNA within chromatin. The figure does not specify cleavage-end chemistry.
operations.information_effect: Chromatin accessibility/protection is encoded as genomic DNA cleavage positions. Cutting is preferential, not a perfectly specific selection of functional regulatory elements. Local cleavage propensity can be sequence-biased.

operations.label: DNA extraction
operations.description: The isolated post-digestion material is converted to a protein-free DNA endpoint, drawn as blue DNA segments. The diagram does not specify the extraction chemistry or adapter construction.
operations.information_effect: The DNA endpoint retains genomic sequence associated with DNase-generated ends, while the depicted extraction removes the protein association. Paper-supported downstream readout, not additional drawn operations: Boyle sequences cut-adjacent DNA tags; Hesselberth sequences the ends of released double-hit fragments. Their genomic locations report cleavage/accessibility; depletion of cleavage relative to accessible flanks can support protected footprints when local sampling is sufficient. DNA reads do not directly identify the bound protein, and DNase sequence bias limits naive interpretation.

method_scopes.rationale: DNase-Seq is explicitly grouped on the middle row. The poster-listed Boyle paper establishes nuclei digestion and recovery of DNase-cut-associated DNA. At this shared schematic scope, o_digest, o_isolate and o_extract apply as digestion, broad recovery and DNA recovery. The corrected meaning of o_isolate is not literal purification of nucleosome-protected DNA. Boyle's Solexa library marks DNase ends with a biotinylated linker containing an MmeI site, recovers cut-adjacent tags through MmeI cleavage/streptavidin enrichment, and supplies a second linker for sequencing. Those paper-only details explain how the library carries cleavage-site information; their internal order is not projected into the cartoon. Other readouts and DNase-chip in the same paper are outside this row.

corrections.diagram_observation: After DNase I digestion, the source says Isolate trimmed complexes and draws separate gray nucleosome-like complexes with short DNA. This could be read as direct enrichment and sequencing of protected nucleosomal DNA.
corrections.primary_statement: Boyle DNase-Seq ligates a biotinylated linker to DNase-generated ends and extracts adjacent DNA tags; its Solexa implementation uses MmeI cleavage and streptavidin enrichment. Hesselberth DNaseI-Seq isolates released short double-hit fragments, whose ends map cleavage sites. Retain the drawn digestion/isolation/extraction route as a shared recovery abstraction, with o_isolate and s_isolated explicitly interpreted from these primary sources. Do not read the nucleosome-like icons as evidence that protected nucleosomal DNA is the selected sequencing target. Protected regions are inferred from relative cleavage patterns, not identified merely by survival or by direct sequencing of purified protein footprints.
